heading: Effect of registration
title: Effect of registration
text: The registration of the company has the following effects: (a) the subscribers to the memorandum, together with such other persons as may from time to time become members of the company, are a body corporate by the name contained in the certificate of incorporation; (b) the body corporate is capable of exercising all the functions of an incorporated company; (c) the status and registered office of the company are as stated in, or in connection with, the application for incorporation; (d) the members of the company have such liability to contribute to the assets of the company in the event of its being wound up as is mentioned in this Act; and (e) the certificate of incorporation shall be conclusive evidence that all the requirements of this Act in respect of registration and of matters precedent and incidental thereto have been complied with.

heading: Pre-incorporation contracts
title: Pre-incorporation contracts
text:
(1) A contract that purports to be made by or on behalf of a company before its incorporation has effect, subject to any agreement to the contrary, as one made with the person purporting to act for the company or as agent for it, and he is personally liable on the contract accordingly.
(2) A company may, within ninety days of its incorporation, adopt a contract made in its name or on its behalf before its incorporation; and upon such adoption: (a) the company shall be bound by and entitled to the benefit thereof as if it had been in existence at the date of such contract and had been a party thereto; and (b) the person who purported to act for the company or as agent for it shall cease to be personally liable on the contract.

heading: Alteration of memorandum
title: Alteration of memorandum
text:
(1) A company may, by special resolution, alter the provisions of its memorandum so as to: (a) change the name of the company; (b) alter the principle line of business; or (c) alter the province of its registered office.
(2) An alteration of the memorandum shall not take effect until it has been confirmed by the Commission on application made within thirty days of the passing of the special resolution.

(2) An alteration of the memorandum shall not take effect until it has been confirmed by the Commission on application made within thirty days of the passing of the special resolution.

heading: Alteration of articles
title: Alteration of articles
text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act and to the conditions contained in its memorandum, a company may, by special resolution, alter or add to its articles.
(2) Any alteration or addition so made shall be as valid as if originally contained in the articles, and be subject in like manner to alteration by special resolution.
(3) A copy of the articles as altered shall, within thirty days from the passing of the resolution, be filed with the registrar.

(3) A copy of the articles as altered shall, within thirty days from the passing of the resolution, be filed with the registrar.

heading: Allotment of shares
title: Allotment of shares
text:
(1) No company shall make any allotment of its shares offered to the public for subscription unless the minimum amount stated in the prospectus has been subscribed and the sum payable on application for the amount so stated has been paid to and received by the company.
(2) Whenever a company makes any allotment of its shares, the company shall within forty-five days thereafter file with the registrar a return of the allotments.

heading: Further issue of capital
title: Further issue of capital
text:
(1) Where the directors decide to increase the capital of the company by the issue of further shares, such shares shall be offered to the members in proportion to the existing shares held by each member (Right Shares).
(2) The offer shall be made by notice specifying the number of shares offered and limiting a time, not being less than fifteen days and not exceeding thirty days from the date of the offer, within which the offer, if not accepted, will be deemed to be declined.
(3) If the offer is declined or not accepted within the time specified, the directors may dispose of the same in such manner as they think fit.

heading: Nature of shares or other interests
title: Nature of shares or other interests
text: The shares or other interest of any member in a company shall be movable property, transferable in the manner provided by the articles of the company.

heading: Classes and kinds of share capital
title: Classes and kinds of share capital
text:
(1) A company having a share capital may have more than one class of shares and may have different rights, privileges and conditions attached to each class as may be specified in its articles.
(2) No company shall issue shares carrying voting rights disproportionate to the paid-up value of shares held.

heading: Records of resolutions and meetings
title: Records of resolutions and meetings
text:
(1) Every company shall cause records of all resolutions and proceedings of general meetings, and of meetings of its directors and board committees, to be kept by being entered in books kept for that purpose within thirty days of the conclusion of each meeting.
(2) Any such minute, if purporting to be signed by the chairman of the meeting at which the proceedings were had, or by the chairman of the next succeeding meeting, shall be evidence of the proceedings.
(3) Where records of the proceedings of any general meeting or of a meeting of directors or committee of directors are kept, until the contrary is proved, the meeting shall be deemed to have been duly held and convened, and all proceedings had thereat to have been duly had, and all appointments of directors, liquidators or other officers shall be deemed to be valid.
(4) The company shall maintain records of all resolutions and minutes for a period of at least twenty years in physical form and permanently in electronic form.

heading: Inspection of minute-books
title: Inspection of minute-books
text:
(1) The books containing the minutes of proceedings of any general meeting of a company shall be kept at the registered office of the company and shall, during business hours (subject to such reasonable restrictions as the company may by its articles or in general meeting impose, so that not less than two hours in each day be allowed for inspection), be open to the inspection of any member without charge.
(2) Any member shall be entitled to be furnished, within seven working days after he has made a request in that behalf to the company, with a certified copy of any minutes referred to in sub-section (1) on payment of such reasonable fee as may be prescribed.
(3) If any inspection required under this section is refused, or if any copy required under this section is not furnished within the specified time, the company and every officer of the company who is in default shall be liable to a penalty of level 1 on the standard scale, and the registrar may by order compel an immediate inspection of the books or direct that the copies required shall be sent to the persons requiring them.

heading: Maintenance and keeping of records in electronic form
title: Maintenance and keeping of records in electronic form
text: Every company shall maintain records of its registers, resolutions, minute books and books of accounts in electronic form in such manner and format as may be specified by the Commission.
text_raw: Every company shall maintain records of its registers, resolutions, minute books and books of accounts in electronic form in such manner and format as may be specified by the Commission.

heading: Power of Court to rectify register
title: Power of Court to rectify register
text:
(1) If: (a) the name of any person is fraudulently, incorrectly or without sufficient cause entered in or omitted from the register of members of a company; or (b) default is made, or unnecessary delay takes place, in entering on the register the fact of any person having become or ceased to be a member; the person aggrieved, or any member of the company, or the company, may apply to the Court for rectification of the register.
(2) The Court may either refuse the application, or may order rectification of the register and payment by the company of any damages sustained by any party aggrieved.
(3) On any application under this section the Court may decide any question relating to the title of any person who is a party to the application to have his name entered in or omitted from the register, whether the question arises between members or alleged members, or between members or alleged members on the one hand and the company on the other hand; and generally may decide any question necessary or expedient to be decided for the rectification of the register.

heading: Trust not to be entered on register
title: Trust not to be entered on register
text: No notice of any trust, expressed, implied or constructive, shall be entered on the register of members, or be receivable by the registrar.
text_raw: No notice of any trust, expressed, implied or constructive, shall be entered on the register of members, or be receivable by the registrar.

heading: Register of members
title: Register of members
text:
(1) Every company shall keep a register of its members, and enter therein: (a) the full name, address, father's or husband's name, nationality and CNIC/passport number of each member; (b) in the case of a company having a share capital, a statement of the shares held by each member; (c) the date at which each person was entered in the register as a member; and (d) the date at which any person ceased to be a member.
(2) If a company makes default in complying with the requirements of this section, the company and every officer of the company who is in default shall be liable to a penalty of level 1 on the standard scale.

(2) If a company makes default in complying with the requirements of this section, the company and every officer of the company who is in default shall be liable to a penalty of level 1 on the standard scale.

heading: Annual general meeting
title: Annual general meeting
text:
(1) Every company shall hold, in addition to any other meetings, a general meeting as its annual general meeting within sixteen months from the date of its incorporation and thereafter once at least in every calendar year within a period of one hundred and twenty days following the close of its financial year.
(2) In the case of a listed company, the Commission, and in any other case, the registrar, may for any special reason extend the time within which any annual general meeting shall be held by a period not exceeding thirty days.

heading: Calling of extraordinary general meeting
title: Calling of extraordinary general meeting
text:
(1) The board may, whenever it thinks fit, call an extraordinary general meeting of the company.
(2) The board shall on the requisition of members representing not less than one-tenth of the voting power on the date of deposit of the requisition, forthwith proceed to call an extraordinary general meeting.
(3) If the board does not proceed within twenty-one days from the date of the deposit of the requisition to call a meeting, the requisitionists, or any of them representing more than one-half of the total voting rights of all of them, may themselves call the meeting within ninety days from the date of the deposit.

heading: Notice of meetings
title: Notice of meetings
text:
(1) A general meeting of a company may be called by giving not less than twenty-one days' notice in writing.
(2) Notice of every general meeting shall be given to every member of the company, to every director, and to the auditor of the company.
(3) The notice of a general meeting shall specify the place and the day and hour of the meeting, and there shall be annexed to the notice of the meeting a statement of the material facts concerning each item of special business to be transacted at the meeting.
(4) In the case of an extraordinary general meeting called upon requisition, the notice shall specify the resolution to be proposed and the business to be transacted.
(5) The accidental omission to give notice to, or the non-receipt of notice by, any member shall not invalidate the proceedings at any meeting.

(5) The accidental omission to give notice to, or the non-receipt of notice by, any member shall not invalidate the proceedings at any meeting.

heading: Quorum of general meeting
title: Quorum of general meeting
text:
(1) Unless the articles provide for a larger number, the quorum of a general meeting shall be: (a) in the case of a public listed company, not less than ten members present personally, or through video-link who represent not less than twenty-five percent of the total voting power; (b) in the case of any other company, not less than two members present personally, or through video-link who represent not less than twenty-five percent of the total voting power; and (c) in the case of a single member company, the single member.
(2) If within half an hour from the time appointed for the meeting a quorum is not present, the meeting, if called upon the requisition of members, shall be dissolved; in any other case, it shall stand adjourned to the same day in the next week.

heading: Power of the Court to call general meeting
title: Power of the Court to call general meeting
text: (1) If for any reason it is impracticable to call a meeting of a company in any manner in which meetings of that company may be called, or to conduct the meeting of the company in the manner prescribed by the articles or this Act, the Court may, either of its own motion or on the application of any director of the company or of any member of the company who would be entitled to vote at the meeting: (a) order a meeting of the company to be called, held and conducted in such manner as the Court thinks fit; and (b) give such ancillary or consequential directions as the Court thinks expedient.

heading: Representation of corporations at meetings
title: Representation of corporations at meetings
text: A body corporate, whether a company within the meaning of this Act or not, may, by resolution of its board or other governing body, authorize such person as it thinks fit to act as its representative at any meeting of any company of which it is a member or creditor.

heading: Proxies
title: Proxies
text:
(1) Any member of a company entitled to attend and vote at a meeting of the company shall be entitled to appoint another person as his proxy to attend, speak and vote instead of him.
(2) A proxy must be a member of the company unless the company's articles permit appointment of a non-member.
(3) The instrument appointing a proxy shall be in writing under the hand of the appointer and must be deposited at the registered office of the company not less than forty-eight hours before the time for holding the meeting.

heading: Ineligibility of certain persons to become director
title: Ineligibility of certain persons to become director
text: A person shall not be eligible for appointment as a director of a company, if he: (a) is a minor; (b) is of unsound mind and stands so declared by a competent court; (c) has applied to be adjudicated as an insolvent and his application is pending; (d) is an undischarged insolvent; (e) has been convicted by a court of law for an offence involving moral turpitude; (f) has been debarred from holding such office under any provision of this Act; (g) has betrayed lack of fiduciary behavior and a declaration to this effect has been made by the Court under section 212 at any time during the preceding five years; (h) does not hold a National Tax Number; (i) is not a member (except in case of chief executive, whole time director or institutional nominee); or (j) has been declared by a court of competent jurisdiction as a defaulter in repayment of loan to a financial institution.

heading: Minimum number of directors
title: Minimum number of directors
text: Every company shall have directors: (a) in the case of a single member company, at least one director; (b) in the case of a private company, not less than two directors; (c) in the case of a public company other than a listed company, not less than three directors; and (d) in the case of a listed company, not less than seven directors.

heading: Number of directorships
title: Number of directorships
text: No person shall hold office as a director, including as an alternate director, at the same time in more than such number of companies as may be specified by the Commission; provided that this limit shall not apply to directorship in a private company which is not a subsidiary of a public company.

heading: Election of directors
title: Election of directors
text:
(1) The directors of a company shall be elected by the members of the company in general meeting in the manner provided in this section.
(2) The board shall fix the number of directors to be elected not later than thirty-five days before the date of the meeting.
(3) Notice of the meeting shall state the number of directors fixed and the names of the retiring directors.
(4) Any member who seeks to contest an election shall lodge with the company a notice of his intention not later than fourteen days before the date of the meeting.

(4) Any member who seeks to contest an election shall lodge with the company a notice of his intention not later than fourteen days before the date of the meeting.

heading: Procedures for election of directors
title: Procedures for election of directors
text:
(1) The directors shall be elected by the members in general meeting by cumulative voting.
(2) A member shall have such number of votes as is equal to the product of the number of voting shares held by him and the number of directors to be elected.
(3) A member may give all his votes to a single candidate or divide them between more than one of the candidates in such manner as he thinks fit.
(4) The candidate who gets the highest number of votes shall be declared elected as director and then the candidate who gets the next highest number of votes and so on until the total number of directors to be elected has been elected.

heading: Circumstances in which election of directors may be declared invalid
title: Circumstances in which election of directors may be declared invalid
text: The Court may, on the application of members holding not less than ten percent of the voting power in the company, made within thirty days from the date of election, declare the election of all or any of the directors invalid if it is satisfied that there has been material irregularity in the holding of the elections and matters incidental thereto.

heading: Independent director
title: Independent director
text:
(1) An independent director means a director who is not connected or does not have any other relationship, whether pecuniary or otherwise, with the company, its associated companies, subsidiaries, holding company or directors.
(2) An independent director shall be selected from a data bank maintained by an institute or body authorized by the Commission.

heading: Disqualification of director by the Commission
title: Disqualification of director by the Commission
text: The Commission may disqualify a person from being appointed or acting as a director of any company for a period not exceeding five years if: (a) he has been convicted of an offence in connection with the promotion, formation or management of a company; (b) he has been guilty of fraud, misfeasance or breach of fiduciary duty; or (c) the company of which he was director became insolvent due to conduct attributable to him.

heading: Vacation of office by director
title: Vacation of office by director
text: (1) A director shall ipso facto cease to hold office if: (a) he becomes ineligible to be a director under section 153; (b) he absents himself from three consecutive meetings of the board without leave of absence; (c) he or any firm of which he is a partner or any private company of which he is a director accepts a loan or guarantee from the company in contravention of section 183; or (d) he fails to disclose his interest in contracts as required under section 205.

heading: Removal of directors
title: Removal of directors
text:
(1) A company may, by resolution in general meeting, remove a director appointed under section 159, 161 or 162.
(2) A resolution to remove a director elected under section 159 shall not be deemed to have been passed if the number of votes cast against it equals or exceeds the minimum number of votes that were necessary to secure his election at the immediately preceding election of directors at which he was elected.
(3) A resolution to remove a director appointed under section 161 shall not be deemed to have been passed if the number of votes cast against it equals or exceeds the number of votes arrived at for election of directors under section 159.
(4) A director nominated by a creditor or institution under section 164 may be removed only by such creditor or institution.

(1) A company may, by resolution in general meeting, remove a director appointed under section 159, 161 or 162.
(2) A resolution to remove a director elected under section 159 shall not be deemed to have been passed if the number of votes cast against it equals or exceeds the minimum number of votes that were necessary to secure his election at the immediately preceding election of directors at which he was elected.

(4) A director nominated by a creditor or institution under section 164 may be removed only by such creditor or institution.

heading: Ineligible person not to act as director
title: Ineligible person not to act as director
text: A person who acts as a director when he is ineligible or disqualified from holding such office shall be liable to a penalty of level 2 on the standard scale and may also be disqualified from holding any directorship for a period of five years.
text_raw: A person who acts as a director when he is ineligible or disqualified from holding such office shall be liable to a penalty of level 2 on the standard scale and may also be disqualified from holding any directorship for a period of five years.

heading: Loans to directors
title: Loans to directors
text: (1) A company shall not make a loan to, or give any guarantee or provide any security in connection with a loan made by any other person to: (a) any director of the company or of its holding company; (b) any of his relatives; (c) any firm in which he or any relative is a partner; or (d) any private company of which he is a director or member; without the approval of the company by special resolution and prior approval of the Commission.

heading: Powers of the Board
title: Powers of the Board
text:
(1) The business of a company shall be managed by the board, who may exercise all such powers of the company as are not required by this Act or by the articles to be exercised by the company in general meeting.
(2) The board of a company shall exercise the following powers on behalf of the company, and the said powers shall be exercised only by means of resolution passed at their meeting, namely: (a) to issue shares; (b) to issue debentures or any other debt security; (c) to borrow money otherwise than on debentures; (d) to invest the funds of the company; (e) to make loans; (f) to authorize a director or the firm of which he is a partner or any partner of such firm to enter into any contract with the company; (g) to approve quarterly, half-yearly and annual financial statements; (h) to approve bonus to employees; (i) to incur capital expenditure on any single item exceeding prescribed thresholds; (j) to undertake obligations under lease exceeding prescribed thresholds; (k) to declare interim dividend; and (l) to write off bad debts, advances and receivables.

heading: Duties of directors
title: Duties of directors
text:
(1) A director of a company shall act in accordance with the articles of the company.
(2) A director of a company shall act in good faith in order to promote the objects of the company for the benefit of its members as a whole, and in the best interests of the company, its employees, the shareholders, the community and for the protection of environment.
(3) A director of a company shall exercise his duties with due and reasonable care, skill and diligence and shall exercise independent judgment.
(4) A director of a company shall not involve in a situation in which he may have a direct or indirect interest that conflicts, or possibly may conflict, with the interest of the company.
(5) A director of a company shall not achieve or attempt to achieve any undue gain or advantage either to himself or to his relatives, partners, or his associates and if such director is found guilty of making any undue gain, he shall be liable to pay an amount equal to that gain to the company.
(6) A director of a company shall not assign his office and any assignment so made shall be void.
(7) A director who contravenes the provisions of this section shall be liable to a penalty of level 2 on the standard scale.

(7) A director who contravenes the provisions of this section shall be liable to a penalty of level 2 on the standard scale.

heading: Disclosure of interest by director
title: Disclosure of interest by director
text:
(1) Every director of a company who is in any way, whether directly or indirectly, concerned or interested in any contract or arrangement entered into, or to be entered into, by or on behalf of the company shall disclose the nature of his concern or interest at a meeting of the board.
(2) In the case of a proposed contract or arrangement, the disclosure shall be made at the meeting of the board at which the question of entering into the contract or arrangement is first taken into consideration.

heading: General notice of interest
title: General notice of interest
text: A general notice given to the board by a director to the effect that he is a director or a member of a specified body corporate or a partner of a specified firm, and is to be regarded as concerned or interested in any contract or arrangement which may, after the date of the notice, be made with that body corporate or firm, shall be deemed to be a sufficient disclosure of interest in relation to any contract or arrangement so made.

heading: Interested director not to participate or vote
title: Interested director not to participate or vote
text: (1) No director of a company shall, as a director, take any part in the discussion of, or vote on, any contract or arrangement entered into, or to be entered into, by or on behalf of the company, if he is in any way, whether directly or indirectly, concerned or interested in the contract or arrangement, nor shall his presence count for the purpose of forming a quorum at the time of any such discussion or vote; and if he does vote, his vote shall be void.

heading: Related party transactions
title: Related party transactions
text:
(1) A company may enter into any contract or arrangement with a related party only in accordance with the policy approved by the board and subject to such terms and conditions as may be specified.
(2) Where a director is interested in any contract or arrangement with a related party, he shall not be present at the meeting during the discussions or voting on such transaction.
(3) Where any contract or arrangement is entered into by a director or any other employee, without obtaining the consent of the board or approval by a special resolution in the general meeting, and if it is not ratified by the board or, as the case may be, by the shareholders at a meeting within ninety days from the date on which such contract or arrangement was entered into, such contract or arrangement shall be voidable at the option of the board.

heading: Register of contracts or arrangements in which directors are interested
title: Register of contracts or arrangements in which directors are interested
text:
(1) Every company shall keep one or more registers in which shall be entered separately particulars of all contracts or arrangements to which section 205, 206 or 208 applies.
(2) The register shall be kept at the registered office and shall be open to the inspection of any member without fee.

heading: Books of account, to be kept by company
title: Books of account, to be kept by company
text:
(1) Every company shall keep at its registered office proper books of account and other relevant books and papers and financial statements for every financial year which give a true and fair view of the state of the affairs of the company.
(2) The books of account shall be preserved in good order for a period of not less than ten years.

heading: Financial statements
title: Financial statements
text:
(1) The board of every company shall lay before the company in annual general meeting financial statements for the period, within one hundred and twenty days following the close of financial year.
(2) The financial statements shall give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the company and comply with the financial reporting framework.

(2) The financial statements shall give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the company and comply with the financial reporting framework.

heading: Approval and signing of financial statements
title: Approval and signing of financial statements
text: (1) The financial statements, including consolidated financial statements, of a company shall be approved by the board and signed on behalf of the board by the chief executive and at least one director of the company, and in the case of a listed company also by the chief financial officer.

heading: Directors' report
title: Directors' report
text:
(1) The board shall make out and attach to every financial statement a report with respect to the state of the company's affairs, the amount of dividend, if any, which it recommends to be paid and the amount which it proposes to carry to any reserve.
(2) The report shall state the principal risks and uncertainties facing the company and contain a fair review of its business.

heading: Dividend to be paid only out of profits
title: Dividend to be paid only out of profits
text:
(1) No dividend shall be paid by a company otherwise than out of profits of the company.
(2) Any dividend declared by a company in general meeting shall be paid within thirty days of the date of declaration.

heading: Unclaimed shares, modaraba certificates and dividend to vest in Federal Government
title: Unclaimed shares, modaraba certificates and dividend to vest in Federal Government
text:
(1) Where any shares, modaraba certificates or other instruments issued by a company remain unclaimed or where any dividend declared remains unpaid for a period of three years from the date of maturity or payment, the company shall give notice to the shareholder or holder of such instrument.
(2) If no claim is preferred within ninety days of the notice, the company shall deposit the unclaimed dividend in the designated account with the Federal Government and deliver the shares, modaraba certificates or other instruments to the Commission.
(3) The shares and dividends so deposited shall vest in the Federal Government.

heading: Appointment of auditors
title: Appointment of auditors
text:
(1) The first auditor or auditors of a company shall be appointed by the board within ninety days of the date of incorporation of the company.
(2) Subsequent auditors shall be appointed by the company at each annual general meeting and shall hold office from the conclusion of that meeting until the conclusion of the next annual general meeting.

heading: Qualification and disqualification of auditors
title: Qualification and disqualification of auditors
text:
(1) A person shall not be qualified for appointment as an auditor of a public company unless he is a chartered accountant within the meaning of the Chartered Accountants Ordinance, 1961.
(2) None of the following persons shall be appointed as an auditor of a company: (a) a person who is, or at any time during the preceding three years was, a director, other officer or employee of the company; (b) a person who is a partner of, or in the employment of, a director, officer or employee of the company; (c) the spouse of a director; or (d) a person indebted to the company.

heading: Investigation into affairs of company
title: Investigation into affairs of company
text: (1) The Commission may appoint one or more competent persons as inspectors to investigate the affairs of any company and to report thereon in such manner as the Commission may direct: (a) on the application of members holding not less than one-tenth of the voting power; (b) on the report of the registrar; or (c) on a special resolution passed by the company that its affairs ought to be investigated.

heading: Compromise or arrangement with creditors and members
title: Compromise or arrangement with creditors and members
text:
(1) Where a compromise or arrangement is proposed between a company and its creditors or any class of them, or between the company and its members or any class of them, the Court may, on the application of the company or of any creditor or member of the company, order a meeting of the creditors or class of creditors, or of the members or class of members, as the case may be, to be called, held and conducted in such manner as the Court directs.
(2) If a majority in number representing three-fourths in value of the creditors or class of creditors, or members or class of members, as the case may be, present and voting either in person or by proxy at the meeting, agree to any compromise or arrangement, the compromise or arrangement shall, if sanctioned by the Court, be binding on all the creditors or the class of creditors, or on the members or the class of members, as the case may be, and also on the company.

heading: Application for prevention of oppression and mismanagement
title: Application for prevention of oppression and mismanagement
text:
(1) If any member or members holding not less than ten percent of the issued share capital of a company, or a creditor or creditors having interest equivalent in amount to not less than ten percent of the paid-up capital of the company, complain, or the Commission is of the opinion, that: (a) the affairs of the company are being conducted, or are likely to be conducted, in a manner prejudicial to public interest or in a manner oppressive to any member or members or in a manner prejudicial to the interests of the company; or (b) any change has taken place in the management or control of the company, whether by an alteration in the board, or of its chief executive, or in the ownership of the company's shares, and that by reason of such change it is likely that the affairs of the company will be conducted in a manner prejudicial to public interest or in a manner oppressive to any member or members; that member or members or, the creditor or creditors, as the case may be, or the Commission may apply to the Court for an order under this section.
(2) An application under sub-section (1) shall be in the form of a petition.
(3) The Court may, on an application under sub-section (1), make such order as it thinks fit with a view to bringing to an end the matters complained of.

heading: Powers of Court on application under section 286
title: Powers of Court on application under section 286
text: (1) Without prejudice to the generality of the powers of the Court under section 286, any order under that section may provide for: (a) the regulation of the conduct of the company's affairs in future; (b) the purchase of the shares or interests of any members of the company by other members or by the company; (c) in the case of a purchase of its shares by the company, the consequent reduction of its share capital; (d) the termination, setting aside or modification of any agreement, howsoever arrived at, between the company and any of its directors, chief executive or other officers; (e) the termination, setting aside or modification of any agreement between the company and any person with respect to management; (f) the setting aside of any fraudulent transfer, delivery of goods, payment, execution or other act relating to property made or done by or against the company within three months before the date of the application; and (g) any other matter for which in the opinion of the Court it is just and equitable that provision should be made.

heading: Interim order
title: Interim order
text: Pending the making by it of a final order under section 286 the Court may, on the application of any party to the proceedings, make any interim order which it thinks fit for regulating the conduct of the company's affairs, upon such terms and conditions as appear to it to be just and equitable.

heading: Effect of alteration of memorandum or articles
title: Effect of alteration of memorandum or articles
text: Where an order under section 286 makes any alteration in the memorandum or articles of a company, then, the company shall not, without the leave of the Court, make any alteration in the memorandum or articles inconsistent with the provisions of the order.
text_raw: Where an order under section 286 makes any alteration in the memorandum or articles of a company, then, the company shall not, without the leave of the Court, make any alteration in the memorandum or articles inconsistent with the provisions of the order.

heading: Termination or modification of certain agreements
title: Termination or modification of certain agreements
text:
(1) Where an order made under section 286 terminates, sets aside or modifies an agreement such as is referred to in clause (d) or (e) of sub-section (1) of section 287: (a) the order shall not give rise to any claim whatever against the company by any person for damages or for compensation for loss of office or in any other respect, either in pursuance of the agreement or otherwise; and (b) no director or other officer of the company whose agreement is so terminated or set aside shall, for a period of five years from the date of the order terminating such agreement, without the leave of the Court, be appointed, or act, as the director, chief executive or other officer of the company.
(2) If any person who has ceased to hold office under an order under section 286 acts as a director, chief executive or other officer of the company without the leave of the Court, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

heading: Power of Commission to file application under section 286
title: Power of Commission to file application under section 286
text: The Commission may, if it considers that the affairs of a company are being conducted in a manner prejudicial to public interest or in a manner oppressive to any member or members, apply to the Court for an order under section 286.

heading: Circumstances in which a company may be wound up by Court
title: Circumstances in which a company may be wound up by Court
text: A company may be wound up by the Court: (a) if the company has, by special resolution, resolved that the company be wound up by the Court; (b) if default is made in delivering the statutory report to the registrar or in holding the statutory meeting; (c) if default is made in holding any two consecutive annual general meetings; (d) if the company does not commence its business within a year from its incorporation, or suspends its business for a whole year; (e) if the number of members is reduced below the statutory minimum; (f) if the company is unable to pay its debts; (g) if the company is: (i) conceived or brought forth for, or is or has been carrying on, unlawful or fraudulent activities; or (ii) carrying on business not authorized by the memorandum; or (iii) conducting its business in a manner oppressive to any of its members or persons concerned with the formation or promotion thereof; or (iv) run and managed by persons who fail to maintain proper accounts; or (h) if the Court is of opinion that it is just and equitable that the company should be wound up.

heading: Application for winding up
title: Application for winding up
text: (1) An application to the Court for the winding up of a company shall be by petition presented, subject to the provisions of this section, either by the company, or by any creditor or creditors, or by any contributory or contributories, or by the registrar or by the Commission.

heading: Penalty for false statement, falsification, and destruction of records
title: Penalty for false statement, falsification, and destruction of records
text: (1) If any person: (a) makes a statement in any return, report, certificate, financial statement, prospectus, resolution or other document, required by or for the purposes of any of the provisions of this Act, which is false in any material particular, knowing it to be false, or omits any material fact, knowing it to be material; or (b) destroys, alters, conceals, falsifies or fabricates any book, paper, register, security, account or other document of the company with intent to defraud or deceive; or (c) makes or abets the making of any false entry or omission in any book, paper or document of the company; he shall be liable to a penalty of level 3 on the standard scale and punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

heading: Penalty for false statement
title: Penalty for false statement
text: Whoever in any return, report, certificate, financial statement, prospectus, offer of shares, books of account or other document required by or for the purposes of any of the provisions of this Act, makes a statement: (a) which is false in any material particular, knowing it to be false; or (b) which omits any material fact knowing it to be material; shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to a fine.

heading: Penalty for wrongful withholding of property
title: Penalty for wrongful withholding of property
text: (1) If any director, officer or other employee of a company wrongfully obtains possession of any property of the company, or having any such property in his possession, wrongfully withholds it or knowingly applies it to purposes other than those expressed or directed in the articles of the company and authorized by this Act, he shall be punishable with fine not exceeding level 2 on the standard scale, and the Court may order him to deliver up or refund within a specified time all such property.
